transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to get the wrap disposition plan locked today so we're clear for Friday's dismantling. Per our standard wrap meeting, I need each department lead to confirm the exact disposition and environmental-compliance requirements for their department. If anyone has an exception to the current draft plan — scenic pieces going to general salvage, selected hero props going to production storage — I need you to state the exact corrective requirement so it can be entered into the meeting record before I can approve. Let's start with any exceptions. Who has one?

transcript.text: I have an exception to the draft plan. The antique jukebox listed as a hero prop is actually a rented piece. I confirmed with the rental house yesterday that its agreement requires it to be returned to the owner in its original condition — it cannot go to production storage or salvage. The corrective requirement is: remove the antique jukebox from the hero props designated for production storage and schedule its return to the rental house owner in original condition before Friday's dismantling.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have an exception to the draft plan. The current draft sends scenic pieces to a general salvage vendor, but our city green-film incentive requires at least 85 percent of dismantled set material by weight to be diverted from landfill. I confirmed with the approved vendor this morning that their audited plan reaches that threshold only through separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record. However, the compliance packet still contains the general-salvage draft. The corrective requirement is: replace the general salvage vendor designation for scenic pieces with the approved recycling vendor's audited plan — separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record — and update the compliance packet to reflect the approved plan before Mara approves the wrap disposition plan.
